+## Accepted result and antecedents
+
+The accepted result is a counterexample to the concrete forward-generation-only
+GNS descent proposal in Michael Skeide's first module-approach problem, OWR
+2009 pp. 542–543 (general definition pp. 497–498), DOI
+[10.4171/OWR/2009/09](https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2009/09).
+The fixed expectation-GNS kernel fails to be invariant at every positive time.
+The small M2/C2 model supplies an explicit nonzero globally positive witness
+at each such time. Failure of descent refutes the offered descent-plus-extension
+conjunction.
+
+The construction's clock/evaluation/translated-unitary mechanism is established
+in Burgarth–Facchi–Hillier, arXiv:2010.00279v2, Ann. Henri Poincaré 24 (2023),
+325–347, [10.1007/s00023-022-01211-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00023-022-01211-y).
+Indeed their earlier amplitude-damping example, after routine compactification
+and forward-generated restriction, already yields this negative phenomenon
+through a short finite-GNS derivation obstruction. Two independent reviewers
+proved that unstated corollary. Their paper is not claimed to have explicitly
+answered the OWR problem.
+
+Dive–Mintert–Burgarth, Phys. Rev. A 92 (2015), 032111,
+[10.1103/PhysRevA.92.032111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.92.032111),
+is the finite-unitary/first-derivative antecedent. Vom Ende's bounded-Hamiltonian
+formulation is cited as related corroboration:
+[10.1142/S1230161223500038](https://doi.org/10.1142/S1230161223500038).
+
+This is an explicit formulation-specific corollary of known clock machinery,
+with a smaller matrix realization and exact positive witnesses. No new general
+dilation method, exhaustive novelty, historical first priority, independent
+historical development or plagiarism finding is asserted. Bounded primary-source
+searches on 13 October 2026 did not locate an explicit earlier publication of the
+exact fixed-GNS source-resolution statement. The same known mechanism also
+gives every-positive-time selfadjoint witnesses in a finite-bath specialization;
+its odd-extension witnesses are not globally positive.
+
+Useful stronger/incomparable sufficient minimality conditions, extension after
+kernel invariance is separately imposed, a normal von Neumann version,
+nonexistence of another dilation and the source's second future-algebra question
+remain outside the result. This is a general C*-dilation, not a strong or
+weak/corner counterexample.
+

+audits and writing. The paper is unrefereed; AI adversarial reviews are not

+## 2. All-time construction: independent verification
+
+Let X be the extended real interval, with endpoints distinguished. It is compact metrizable, for example using the extension of the arctangent metric. Translation by any finite real number fixes the endpoints and is a homeomorphism. Moreover, its displacement in that metric is bounded uniformly in x by the absolute translation amount. Consequently translation acts point-norm continuously on C(X,M2).
+
+The function g in the proof is continuous: its positive-side limit at zero is zero, its limit at positive infinity is pi/4, and it is zero on the negative half-line and at negative infinity. No derivative at zero is required. Thus V(x)=R(g(x)) is a continuous unitary-valued function.
+
+There is an independent way to verify all cocycle and continuity assertions at once. Set eta(f)(x)=V(x)f(x)V(x)* and let tau_t be translation. Then
+
+    alpha_t = eta^(-1) tau_t eta.
+
+This is exactly the packet's formula. Therefore alpha is an automorphism group, including negative times, and is point-norm continuous because eta is an isometric *-automorphism. Equivalently, direct cancellation proves u_s(x)u_t(x+s)=u_(s+t)(x). No commutation assumption on the matrices is required for that cancellation.
+
+The C*-algebra A generated by alpha_r(D), r>=0, contains the ambient identity, is separable as a C*-subalgebra of the separable ambient algebra, and is invariant under every alpha_t for t>=0. Continuity, multiplicativity, preservation of adjoints, and preservation of the unit all survive restriction. Injectivity survives because alpha_t is injective on the larger algebra. Surjectivity of its restriction is unnecessary.
+
+This choice of A proves precisely the requested forward-generation condition. It does not rely on extra, unobserved summands of the ambient algebra. It also makes A the smallest forward-invariant closed *-subalgebra of the ambient system containing D. This statement concerns generation, not another theory's stronger Markov-dilation minimality.

+## 3. Inclusion, expectation, and Markov maps
+
+The inclusion i identifies C^2 with constant diagonal matrices. It is an isometric unital *-embedding. Evaluation at zero is a unital *-homomorphism. Diagonal extraction has the Kraus formula
+
+    Delta(z) = q z q + (1-q) z (1-q),
+
+so it is completely positive and unital. Their composite p is therefore UCP. For diagonal b and c, p(i(b)fi(c))=b p(f)c, while p i=id. Hence i p is a norm-one, positive, idempotent bimodule projection onto i(C^2), as required. Its range lies in A because D is already contained in A.
+
+At x=0, u_t(0)=R(g(t)) for every t>=0. The two diagonal entries after conjugation have coefficients cos^2(g(t)) and sin^2(g(t)), equal respectively to (1+exp(-t))/2 and (1-exp(-t))/2. Thus the displayed P_t is valid at every nonnegative time. Writing P_t=J+exp(-t)H, the identities J^2=J, H^2=H, JH=HJ=0 prove the semigroup law for all real s,t>=0. Its entries are nonnegative and each row sums to one. Complete positivity follows either from the UCP compression formula or positivity on C^2. Analytic dependence of P_t proves uniform continuity of the Markov semigroup.
+
+Point-norm continuity of theta is sufficient here; the proof never needs uniform continuity of theta as a map into the operator norm on all bounded maps. The square-root behavior of g near zero introduces no continuity defect.

+## 4. GNS correspondence and representation kernel
+
+For z,w in M2, the module inner product Delta(z*w) records the ordinary inner products of corresponding columns. Therefore its norm is the maximum of the two column norms. It is definite and complete, and the right action is multiplication by diagonal matrices. Left multiplication by an evaluated matrix is bounded and has left multiplication by its adjoint as adjoint. The vector xi=I has inner product 1.
+
+For s=log 2, evaluation of theta_s(q) at zero is the rank-one projection Q with entries 3/4, sqrt(3)/4, sqrt(3)/4, and 1/4. Together q, 1-q, and Q generate all four matrix units: qQ(1-q)=(sqrt(3)/4)e12, and taking its adjoint produces e21. Thus evaluation of A at zero is all of M2. It follows that A xi D spans the claimed module. The canonical GNS construction is therefore unitarily identifiable with this concrete cyclic correspondence.
+
+The left representation is exactly left multiplication by f(0). It vanishes precisely when f(0)=0. In particular, this is the kernel of the entire representation, a closed two-sided ideal, not just the null space of the expectation or a single scalar state. Conversely, faithfulness of Delta on positive matrices already implies that p(f*f)=0 forces f(0)=0 in this example. No faithfulness of p on A is inferred.
+
+The two column spaces are the components selected by the central minimal projections of D. Every adjointable D-linear operator preserves them, so B^a(E)=M2 direct-sum M2. The image pi(A) is the diagonal copy of M2. Also pi i is faithful on D. The module is full because its inner products include 1_D. None of these additional favorable features restores kernel invariance.

+

+
+After applying theta_s and evaluating at zero, the result is d Q. Hence

+    p theta_s(a) = d diag(3/4,1/4) != 0.

+## 6. Additional independent stress test: failure at every positive time
+
+The obstruction is not an isolated radical coincidence. For any s>0, put r=exp(-s) and define
+
+    a_s = q theta_s(q) q - ((1+r)/2) q.
+
+The same evaluation argument gives pi(a_s)=0. Using cos(2g(s))=r and cos(2g(2s))=r^2 yields
+
+    a_s(s) = d_s q,
+    d_s = ((1-r^2)/2) (sqrt(1+r^2)-r) > 0,
+    p theta_s(a_s) = d_s diag((1+r)/2,(1-r)/2).
+
+Indeed cos(2(g(2s)-g(s)))=r^3+(1-r^2)sqrt(1+r^2), which immediately gives this expression. Positivity is strict for every 0<r<1.

+Even the witnesses themselves can be chosen positive. On the positive half-line,

+    g'(x) = 1/(2 sqrt(exp(2x)-1)),

+## 7. Adversarial objections and their disposition
+
+- Hidden strongness assumption: absent from the source's general definition; the witness explicitly violates strongness.
+- Hidden corner condition: absent. With unital i, a weak/corner dilation here would force the corner to be all of A, which is incompatible with this nontrivial expectation.
+- Unrelated ambient summand: eliminated by the actual definition of A from forward translates.
+- Incorrect representation kernel: ruled out by the explicit faithful evaluated left action and cyclicity.
+- Nonfaithful observed algebra: ruled out by the constant inclusion and faithful pi i.
+- Discrete-time-only construction: ruled out by automorphism conjugacy with real translation and the all-time exponential compression formula.
+- Failure at compactification endpoints: ruled out by endpoint continuity and translation fixing both endpoints.
+- Missing complete positivity: ruled out by the Kraus/evaluation formula at every matrix level.
+- Failure of injectivity or unitality after restriction: neither occurs.
+- Nonseparable dilation algebra: A lies in a separable ambient C*-algebra.
+- Reliance on a noncyclic module: matrix-unit generation proves cyclicity.
+- Wrong interpretation of B^a(E): the right D-module has two independent columns, giving M2 direct-sum M2.
+- Replacing this dilation by a better one: irrelevant to the fixed-dilation universal assertion.
+- Treating finite exact tests as the analytic proof: not done; all-time arguments are supplied separately above.
+- Importing W*-normality or continuity by bidualization: not done and not needed.

+import hashlib,json,pathlib,sys
+here=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+manifest=json.loads((here/'AUDIT_SHA256SUMS.json').read_text())

+# A generated continuous dilation whose GNS kernel is not invariant
+
+## Result and precise scope
+
+There is a unital, separable C*-algebra A, a point-norm continuous semigroup
+(theta_t)_{t >= 0} of injective unital *-endomorphisms of A, a unital embedding
+of B = C^2 into A, and a conditional expectation p: A -> B such that:
+
+1. A = C*(theta_t(B): t >= 0);
+2. T_t = p theta_t|_B is the uniformly continuous two-state Markov semigroup
+   with transition matrix
+
+       P_t = (1/2) [[1 + exp(-t), 1 - exp(-t)],
+                    [1 - exp(-t), 1 + exp(-t)]];
+
+3. if pi is the left action in the GNS B-correspondence of p, then
+   theta_s(ker pi) is not contained in ker pi for s = log 2.
+
+Consequently no maps on pi(A), or on all adjointable operators of that fixed
+GNS module, can intertwine pi with this dilation. Generation by the observed
+algebra and its forward time shifts does not suffice for the two-stage
+GNS-extension proposal in OWR-3392-012.
+
+This is a counterexample to that universal generation-only assertion. It does
+not claim that, whenever kernel-invariance is separately assumed, every
+induced endomorphism semigroup fails to extend. Nor does it rule out stronger
+conditions involving the expectation, a corner dilation, a different GNS
+module, or a different dilation of the same Markov semigroup. Any condition
+logically weaker than the generation hypothesis alone also cannot suffice:
+this example satisfies the generation hypothesis itself.
+
+## 1. Continuous ambient dynamics
+
+Let X = [-infinity,+infinity] be the two-point compactification of the real
+line, with its order topology. This is a compact metrizable space. Write
+C = C(X,M_2(C)). Put
+
+    g(x) = 0                                      for x <= 0,
+    g(x) = (1/2) arccos(exp(-x))                   for x > 0,
+    g(-infinity) = 0,     g(+infinity) = pi/4.
+
+This defines a continuous real-valued function on X. For a real angle z let
+
+    R(z) = [[cos z, -sin z], [sin z, cos z]],
+    V(x) = R(g(x)).
+
+For t in R, translation x -> x+t fixes both endpoints of X. It is a
+homeomorphism, and (t,x) -> x+t is jointly continuous on R x X. Set
+
+    u_t(x) = V(x)* V(x+t),
+    alpha_t(f)(x) = u_t(x) f(x+t) u_t(x)*.
+
+The cocycle equality
+
+    u_s(x) u_t(x+s) = V(x)* V(x+s) V(x+s)* V(x+s+t)
+                    = u_(s+t)(x)
+
+proves alpha_s alpha_t = alpha_(s+t). Each alpha_t is a unital
+*-automorphism of C, with inverse alpha_(-t).
+
+For completeness, this group is point-norm continuous. For a fixed f in C,
+the function (t,x) -> u_t(x) f(x+t) u_t(x)* is jointly continuous. On every
+compact t-interval times X it is uniformly continuous, so its supremum-norm
+variation tends to zero as t tends to any fixed t_0. This is continuity of
+t -> alpha_t(f); uniform continuity of t -> alpha_t in operator norm is not
+needed or asserted.
+
+## 2. Enforce exactly the proposed generation condition
+
+Let D be the constant diagonal matrices in C, identified with B = C^2.
+Define the C*-subalgebra
+
+    A = C*(alpha_r(D): r >= 0)  contained in C.
+
+This is unital and separable. For every t >= 0,
+alpha_t(alpha_r(D)) = alpha_(t+r)(D), hence alpha_t(A) is contained in A.
+Let theta_t be this restriction. It is unital, injective, and point-norm
+continuous, since it is the restriction of alpha_t. Surjectivity on A is
+not needed. By the definition of A,
+
+    A = C*(theta_r(D): r >= 0).
+
+Thus there is no added independent algebraic summand: every element of A is
+norm-approximated by *-polynomials in the observed time translates. The
+ambient algebra C is only a construction device; the dilation algebra is A.
+
+Let Delta: M_2(C) -> D denote diagonal extraction and define
+
+    p(f) = Delta(f(0)),
+    i(b) = the constant diagonal matrix b.
+
+Evaluation at 0 is a unital *-homomorphism, and Delta is unital completely
+positive. Thus p is unital completely positive. Moreover p i = id_D, and
+p(i(b_1) f i(b_2)) = b_1 p(f) b_2. Consequently i p is a positive,
+contractive, idempotent D-bimodule projection of A onto i(D): it is a
+conditional expectation. This verifies the source's general-dilation
+condition, with the expectation oriented A -> B.
+
+## 3. The compression is a genuine Markov semigroup
+
+At x=0 and t>=0, V(0)=1 and u_t(0)=R(g(t)). For b=diag(b_1,b_2),
+
+    p theta_t(b)
+      = diag(cos^2(g(t)) b_1 + sin^2(g(t)) b_2,
+             sin^2(g(t)) b_1 + cos^2(g(t)) b_2).
+
+Because cos(2g(t))=exp(-t), this is exactly the matrix P_t in the theorem.
+If J=(1/2)[[1,1],[1,1]] and K=(1/2)[[1,-1],[-1,1]], then
+J^2=J, K^2=K and JK=KJ=0, so
+
+    P_s P_t = (J+exp(-s)K)(J+exp(-t)K)
+            = J+exp(-(s+t))K = P_(s+t).
+
+The P_t are positive stochastic matrices, hence unital completely positive
+maps on C^2, and P_0 is the identity. Their entries vary continuously, even
+analytically, with t. Thus (A,theta,i,p) is a unital dilation of a genuine
+uniformly continuous Markov semigroup for every real t>=0, not only at a
+single time or at integer times.
+
+## 4. Identify the GNS representation kernel
+
+The Hilbert D-module M_2(C), with right action by diagonal multiplication and
+D-valued inner product
+
+    <z,w> = Delta(z* w),
+
+is a concrete GNS correspondence for p once A acts by f.z = f(0)z and the
+cyclic vector is xi=I_2. The inner product is definite: if Delta(z*z)=0,
+both columns of z have squared norm zero, so z=0. It is complete because
+it is finite-dimensional.
+
+To verify cyclicity, let q=diag(1,0) and choose s=log 2. Since
+exp(-s)=1/2, g(s)=pi/6, and the evaluation of theta_s(q) at 0 is
+
+    Q = [[3/4, sqrt(3)/4], [sqrt(3)/4, 1/4]].
+
+The evaluation image of A contains q, I_2 and Q. It therefore contains
+q Q (I_2-q)=(sqrt(3)/4)e_12 and its adjoint, as well as the two diagonal
+matrix units. It is all of M_2(C). Hence A xi D spans this module.
+
+The canonical left representation is therefore
+
+    pi(f)z = f(0)z,
+    ker pi = {f in A: f(0)=0}.
+
+This is the representation kernel, not merely the null space of a single
+vector state. One can also check it without identifying the module: if
+f(0)=0, then p(h* f* f h)=0 for every h in A, so pi(f)=0; conversely
+pi(f)=0 implies p(f*f)=0 and thus f(0)=0 by faithfulness of Delta on
+positive 2x2 matrices.
+
+The module is full, since <xi,xi>=1_D. Its adjointable operators are
+B^a(E) = M_2(C) direct-sum M_2(C), acting separately on the two columns.
+Under this identification pi(A) is the diagonal copy {(z,z):z in M_2(C)}.
+Fullness and finite-dimensionality of the GNS module do not prevent the
+obstruction below.
+
+## 5. An exact element that leaves the kernel
+
+Retain s=log 2 and put q_s=theta_s(q). The self-adjoint element
+
+    a = q q_s q - (3/4)q
+
+belongs to A. From Q above, a(0)=0, so pi(a)=0.
+
+At the point x=s, the cocycle angle for theta_s is
+
+    delta = g(2s)-g(s)
+          = (1/2)arccos(1/4) - pi/6.
+
+Thus q q_s(s) q=cos^2(delta)q. The angle-difference identity gives
+
+    cos(2 delta)
+      = cos(arccos(1/4)-pi/3)
+      = (1+3 sqrt(5))/8,
+
+and therefore
+
+    cos^2(delta) = (9+3 sqrt(5))/16,
+    a(s) = d q,      d = (3 sqrt(5)-3)/16 > 0.
+
+Applying theta_s and evaluating at 0 now gives
+
+    (theta_s(a))(0) = R(pi/6) a(s) R(pi/6)* = d Q != 0.
+
+In particular
+
+    p theta_s(a) = d diag(3/4,1/4) != 0.
+
+Hence theta_s(a) is not in ker pi, although a is. The kernel is not invariant.
+
+If endomorphisms beta_t on pi(A) satisfied beta_t(pi(f))=pi(theta_t(f)), the choice
+f=a would yield beta_s(0)=pi(theta_s(a))!=0. Thus there is no induced
+endomorphism at this time. In particular, there cannot be an E0-semigroup
+on B^a(E) restricting to the specified represented dynamics. The obstruction
+occurs before any product-system classification or extension theorem can
+apply.
+
+## 6. Hypotheses that must not be silently added
+
+- The construction is in the C*-algebra setting explicitly permitted by the
+  source. It makes no claim about a normal, strongly continuous von Neumann
+  version. Merely taking biduals would require a new continuity check.
+- The maps theta_t are injective and point-norm continuous; the Markov maps
+  T_t are uniformly continuous. There is no discrete-time loophole.
+- The expectation p is not faithful; that is allowed in the source, whose
+  first stage explicitly concerns a nonfaithful GNS representation. Imposing
+  faithfulness of p would remove this particular first-stage obstruction.
+- This is a general unital dilation, not a weak/corner dilation. If it were
+  weak with unital i, its corner projection would be 1 and p would be the
+  identity on A, which it is not.
+- It is not strong in the sense p theta_t = T_t p on all A: the witness has
+  p(a)=0 but p theta_s(a)!=0. The source's displayed definition of a general
+  dilation does not impose this extra equation.
+- Algebraic generation is different from uniqueness or minimality of a
+  Markov dilation with specified multitime moments. Those stronger notions
+  cannot be imported from a theorem about a different dilation category.
+- The ambient dynamics uses the explicit continuous unitary cocycle u_t.
+  This is a construction of the given dilation, not a claim that cocycle
+  conjugacy permits replacing it when asking for its fixed GNS extension.
+- No product system is assumed. A product-system existence theorem that
+  constructs some dilation of T does not prove that this particular theta
+  descends through this particular pi.
+
+A useful necessary compatibility condition for any revised proposal is
+precisely that, for every a in A,
+
+    [p(h* a* a h)=0 for all h in A]
+       implies
+    [p(h* theta_t(a)* theta_t(a) h)=0 for all h in A].
+
+This is an exact reformulation of GNS-kernel invariance, not a new sufficient
+minimality theorem and not a resolution of the conditional extension problem.
+A condition weaker than forward generation alone cannot repair the failure;
+a successful replacement must add a restriction not satisfied here. The
+search for broadly useful stronger conditions is left open.
+
+## Sources and status
+
+The target is the first problem in Michael Skeide's section on the module
+approach, pp. 542-543 of *Mini-Workshop: Product Systems and Independence in
+Quantum Dynamics*, Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), 493-548,
+[DOI 10.4171/OWR/2009/09](https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2009/09).
+The general-dilation definition used here is on pp. 497-498 of the same report.
+The report's reversed domain/codomain in the problem's expectation notation is
+resolved using that definition and its diagram.
+
+The distinction between general, strong, and weak dilations is also explicit
+in Appendix B(i), pp. 211-213 of the inspected v3 of Shalit and Skeide,
+*CP-Semigroups and Dilations, Subproduct Systems and Superproduct Systems:
+The Multi-Parameter Case and Beyond*,
+[arXiv:2003.05166v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05166v3), later published in
+Dissertationes Mathematicae 585 (2023),
+[DOI 10.4064/dm823-5-2022](https://doi.org/10.4064/dm823-5-2022).
+That work distinguishes its weak-dilation theorems from general dilations;
+its abstract is not a resolution certificate for the present question.
+
+This document supplies an explicit candidate counterexample, not a verified
+claim of literature priority. Bounded literature searches found no earlier
+matching resolution. Independent mathematical and source review is required
+before accepting the candidate.
+
+A later related formulation is in Section 5, p. 34 of Skeide and Sumesh,
+*CP-H-Extendable Maps between Hilbert modules and CPH-Semigroups*,
+[arXiv:1210.7491v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7491v2), subsequently published
+in J. Math. Anal. Appl. 414 (2014), 886-913,
+[DOI 10.1016/j.jmaa.2014.01.024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmaa.2014.01.024).
+The inspected passage raises the general GNS-extension question; it is not
+used as a theorem establishing either a positive or negative answer.

+\title{Forward generation does not ensure GNS descent:\\an explicit continuous counterexample}
+\author{Alec Kriebel\\Independent researcher\\
+\small\href{https://orcid.org/0009-0001-9320-500X}{ORCID: 0009-0001-9320-500X}}
+\date{13 October 2026}

+\maketitle
+\begin{abstract}
+For a general conditional-expectation dilation of a Markov semigroup,
+generation by the observed algebra and its forward translates does not
+ensure descent through the expectation's fixed GNS representation. We give
+a unital separable, injective, point-norm continuous example for the
+two-state exponential relaxation semigroup. Its GNS image is $M_2(\C)$,
+and at every positive time an explicit nonzero positive element leaves
+the representation kernel. This refutes the concrete generation-only
+proposal in Skeide's 2009 module-approach problem. The clock/cocycle
+method is established: the negative phenomenon is also a short corollary
+of an earlier clock dilation of Burgarth, Facchi and Hillier. The note
+makes the connection explicit and supplies a small matrix realization
+with exact witnesses; it makes no claim of literature-first priority.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\paragraph{Disclosure.}
+AI tools were used extensively in constructing, checking, auditing and
+writing this work. This is an unrefereed research note; its adversarial
+reviews were performed by AI tools and do not constitute human peer review.
+
+\section*{The question and the result}
+In the first module-approach problem of \cite[pp.~542--543]{owr}, Skeide
+proposes passing a general dilation $(A,\theta,i,p)$ through the GNS
+correspondence of $p$, and then extending its represented dynamics to all
+adjointable operators. Generation of $A$ by $i(B)$ and its time translates
+is offered as a sufficient ``not too big'' condition. We use the report's
+general definition \cite[pp.~497--498]{owr}: $ip$ is a conditional
+expectation onto $i(B)$ and $p\theta_t i=T_t$. The printed direction of
+$p$ in the problem is reversed; the definition and diagrams specify
+$p:A\to B$. The stronger equation $p\theta_t=T_t p$ on all of $A$ is
+not assumed.
+
+Let $\D\subset M_2(\C)$ be the diagonal algebra, identified with $\C^2$,
+and let $\Delta:M_2(\C)\to\D$ extract the diagonal.
+\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
+There exist a unital separable C*-algebra $A$, a point-norm continuous
+semigroup $(\theta_t)_{t\geq0}$ of injective unital *-endomorphisms,
+a unital embedding $i:\D\to A$, and a conditional expectation
+$ip:A\to i(\D)$ such that
+\[
+ A=C^*(\theta_r(i(\D)):r\geq0),\qquad
+ T_t=p\theta_t i,\qquad
+ P_t=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1+e^{-t}&1-e^{-t}\\1-e^{-t}&1+e^{-t}\end{pmatrix}
+\]
+is the transition matrix of $T_t$ on $\C^2$.
+For the left representation $\pi$ in the GNS correspondence of $p$,
+\[
+ \pi(A)\cong M_2(\C),\qquad
+ \theta_s(\ker\pi)\not\subseteq\ker\pi\quad\text{for every }s>0.
+\]
+Each failure has an explicit nonzero positive witness $a_s\in\ker\pi$.
+Consequently no semigroup on that represented algebra, or on all
+$\Ba(E)$ of the fixed GNS correspondence, can intertwine $\pi$ and $\theta$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\section*{Construction and proof}
+Let $X=[-\infty,+\infty]$ be the two-endpoint compactification of $\R$
+with its order topology. Define
+\[
+ g(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\leq0,\\\tfrac12\arccos(e^{-x}),&x>0,\end{cases}
+ \qquad g(-\infty)=0,\quad g(+\infty)=\pi/4,
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ R(z)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos z&-\sin z\\\sin z&\cos z\end{pmatrix},
+ \qquad V(x)=R(g(x)),\qquad u_t(x)=V(x)^*V(x+t).
+\]
+Translation fixes the endpoints of $X$. It is jointly continuous in
+$(t,x)$: for time in a bounded neighborhood, sufficiently far tails
+remain in any prescribed endpoint neighborhood. Thus, on $C(X,M_2(\C))$,
+\[
+ \alpha_t(f)(x)=u_t(x)f(x+t)u_t(x)^*,\qquad t\in\R,
+\]
+defines a point-norm continuous automorphism group. Indeed
+$u_s(x)u_t(x+s)=u_{s+t}(x)$, and joint continuity on compact time
+intervals times $X$ gives uniform continuity for each fixed $f$.
+No differentiability of $g$ at zero is required.
+
+View $\D$ as the constant diagonal functions and set
+\[
+ A=C^*(\alpha_r(\D):r\geq0),\quad
+ \theta_t=\alpha_t|_A\ (t\geq0),\quad i(b)(x)=b,\quad
+ p(f)=\Delta(f(0)).
+\]
+The shift of a generator at $r$ is the generator at $r+t$, so $A$ is
+forward invariant and the asserted generation equality is exact.
+Restrictions of the ambient automorphisms are injective unital
+endomorphisms. Norm continuity allows rational times to generate $A$,
+proving separability. Evaluation and $\Delta$ are unital completely
+positive; $pi=\mathrm{id}_{\D}$ and
+$p(i(b_1)fi(b_2))=b_1p(f)b_2$. Hence $ip$ is a conditional expectation.
+
+At $x=0$, $u_t(0)=R(g(t))$ for $t\geq0$. Compressing a constant
+diagonal matrix gives weights
+$\cos^2 g(t)=(1+e^{-t})/2$ and $\sin^2 g(t)=(1-e^{-t})/2$.
+These are precisely $P_t$. Writing
+\[
+ J=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+ K=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_t=J+e^{-t}K,
+\]
+we have $J^2=J$, $K^2=K$, $JK=KJ=0$ and $J+K=I$.
+This proves the Markov semigroup law for every real $t\geq0$.
+The maps are UCP and uniformly continuous on $\C^2$.
+
+\paragraph{The actual GNS representation.}
+Let $q=\diag(1,0)$ and $s_0=\log2$. Evaluation of
+$\theta_{s_0}(q)$ at zero is
+\[
+ Q=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&\sqrt3/4\\\sqrt3/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+The evaluation image contains $q$, $1-q$, $qQ(1-q)=(\sqrt3/4)e_{12}$
+and its adjoint. Therefore $\ev_0(A)=M_2(\C)$.
+The GNS correspondence is concretely
+\[
+ E=M_2(\C),\qquad z\cdot b=zb,\qquad
+ \langle z,w\rangle=\Delta(z^*w),\qquad \xi=I_2,\qquad
+ \pi(f)z=f(0)z.
+\]
+To verify this, the map $a\otimes b\mapsto a(0)b$ on the algebraic
+GNS construction preserves its inner product. The concrete inner
+product is definite because its diagonal entries are column squared
+norms, and the evaluation image proves surjectivity and cyclicity.
+Finite dimension gives completeness. In particular,
+\[
+ \ker\pi=\{f\in A:f(0)=0\}.
+\]
+This is the full representation kernel, not an identification with a
+single vector-state null space in general. The two columns identify
+$\Ba(E)=M_2(\C)\oplus M_2(\C)$; $\pi(A)$ is the diagonal copy.
+The module is full since $\langle\xi,\xi\rangle=1_{\D}$.
+
+\paragraph{A positive witness at every positive time.}
+Fix $s>0$, put $r=e^{-s}\in(0,1)$ and $Q_s=\theta_s(q)(0)$, and define
+\[
+ a_s=q\theta_s(q)q-\frac{1+r}{2}q.
+\]
+Then $a_s\in A$ and $a_s(0)=0$. At $x=s$ its coefficient of $q$ is
+\begin{align*}
+ d_s&=\cos^2(g(2s)-g(s))-\frac{1+r}{2}\\
+ &=\frac{r^3+(1-r^2)\sqrt{1+r^2}-r}{2}
+ =\frac{(1-r^2)(\sqrt{1+r^2}-r)}{2}>0.
+\end{align*}
+Here the angle-difference identity uses
+$\cos(2g(s))=r$, $\cos(2g(2s))=r^2$, and their positive sines.
+Consequently
+\[
+ \theta_s(a_s)(0)=d_s Q_s\ne0.
+\]
+Moreover $a_s$ is positive everywhere. For $x>0$,
+$g'(x)=1/(2\sqrt{e^{2x}-1})$ is positive and decreasing. Comparing
+its integrals on $[x,x+s]$ and $[0,s]$ gives
+$0\leq g(x+s)-g(x)\leq g(s)$. For $x\leq0$ the same bound follows
+from monotonicity and $g(x)=0$, and at the endpoints the increment is
+zero. Since $\cos^2$ decreases on $[0,\pi/4]$,
+\[
+ a_s(x)=\left(\cos^2(g(x+s)-g(x))-\cos^2g(s)\right)q\geq0.
+\]
+Strict positivity of $d_s$ proves $a_s\ne0$. At $s=\log2$,
+$d_s=3(\sqrt5-1)/16$, giving an exact radical witness.
+An intertwining map would send both $\pi(0)$ and $\pi(a_s)$ to the
+same value while their required images are $0$ and $d_s Q_s$.
+This proves the theorem.

+\section*{Antecedents and the finite-image obstruction}
+The point-localized clock and translated-unitary construction are
+established in the cited arXiv v2 of Burgarth--Facchi--Hillier (BFH)
+\cite[Definition~4.1, Theorem~4.4, Step~2, equation~(11)]{bfh}.
+Finite time-dependent unitary dilations and their initial square-root
+singularities are treated by Dive--Mintert--Burgarth
+\cite[Method, Appendices~A--B, arXiv~v3]{dmb}. Their first-derivative
+obstruction has a bounded-total-Hamiltonian formulation in the cited
+arXiv v3 of \cite[Theorem~1]{ende}.
+The following elementary conditional-expectation version explains the
+connection; it is proved here rather than attributed to those papers
+as a fixed-GNS theorem.
+
+\begin{proposition}\label{prop:finite}
+For a point-norm continuous general unital dilation of a norm-continuous
+Markov semigroup on a finite-dimensional algebra $B$, if $\pi(A)$ is
+finite dimensional and $\ker\pi$ is invariant at every time, then the
+generator of the compressed semigroup is a *-derivation on $B$.
+\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}
+Kernel invariance gives a continuous endomorphism semigroup $\beta_t$
+on $C=\pi(A)$. Finite dimension makes continuity operator-norm
+continuity. For small $h>0$, $S=\int_0^h\beta_u\,du$ is invertible
+because $S/h\to I$. The identity
+$\beta_tS=\int_t^{t+h}\beta_u\,du$ proves right differentiability
+at zero. Its generator $\delta$ is a *-derivation by differentiation
+of multiplicativity. The embedding $j=\pi i$ is faithful, and
+$\bar p(c)=\langle\xi,c\xi\rangle$ is a $B$-bimodule UCP map
+with $\bar p j=\mathrm{id}_B$. Thus, identifying $B$ with $j(B)$,
+\[
+ L(bc)=\bar p(\delta(bc))=\bar p(\delta(b))c+b\bar p(\delta(c))
+       =L(b)c+bL(c).
+\]
+Adjoints are preserved as well.
+\end{proof}
+
+In fact BFH's earlier explicit amplitude-damping clock already yields
+the negative generation-only conclusion as a short corollary. The model
+is in Section~2, equations~(1)--(3), of the cited arXiv v2 of \cite{bfh}.
+Its finite unitary path has angle
+\[
+ G(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(x)\arccos(e^{-|x|/2}),\qquad G(0)=0,
+\]
+with finite endpoint limits.
+It therefore extends to $[-\infty,+\infty]$, where its translated
+cocycle is point-norm continuous. Restriction to the forward-generated
+observable algebra preserves the conditional expectation and the
+compression. Evaluation followed by finite bath compression gives a
+finite-dimensional GNS image. The decaying-level projection satisfies
+$T_t(q)=e^{-t}q$, whereas a derivation satisfies $qL(q)q=0$.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} rules out invariance at all times.
+The generic strong continuity of BFH's Hilbert-space unitaries alone
+would not justify point-norm continuity on all $C_b(\R)$; the endpoint
+check for this explicit path is essential.
+
+Thus the general negative phenomenon is not a new clock-dilation
+mechanism. Theorem~\ref{thm:main} gives a small $M_2/\C^2$ realization
+and positive witnesses at every positive time. Bounded primary-source
+searches through 13 October 2026 found no publication explicitly stating
+the exact OWR fixed-GNS counterexample, but neither that search nor the
+explicit refinement certifies first priority. Full source locations,
+hashes and the prior-result deduction are in the verification package.
+
+\section*{Scope and reproducibility}
+This answers negatively the concrete forward-generation-only proposal
+in \cite{owr}. Failure of its first step refutes the proposed two-step

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Integrity rejection controls in disposable copies, normal and optimized Python."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+CASES = ['intact', 'changed_bytes', 'missing_file', 'unexpected_file',
+         'empty_inventory', 'duplicate_entry', 'path_traversal', 'absolute_path',
+         'wrong_size', 'wrong_hash', 'duplicate_json_key', 'symlink',
+         'unexpected_directory']
+
+
+def mutate(root, case):
+    mf = root / 'PUBLICATION_MANIFEST.json'
+    m = json.loads(mf.read_text())
+    target = root / 'packet/PROOF.md'
+    if case == 'intact': return
+    if case == 'changed_bytes': target.write_bytes(target.read_bytes() + b'!'); return
+    if case == 'missing_file': target.unlink(); return
+    if case == 'unexpected_file': (root / 'EXTRA.txt').write_text('extra'); return
+    if case == 'symlink': target.unlink(); target.symlink_to(root / 'README.md'); return
+    if case == 'unexpected_directory': (root / 'extra').mkdir(); return
+    if case == 'duplicate_json_key':
+        mf.write_text(mf.read_text().replace('"schema":', '"schema": "duplicate", "schema":', 1)); return
+    if case == 'empty_inventory': m['files'] = []
+    if case == 'duplicate_entry': m['files'][1] = m['files'][0].copy()
+    if case == 'path_traversal': m['files'][0]['path'] = '../README.md'
+    if case == 'absolute_path': m['files'][0]['path'] = '/tmp/README.md'
+    if case == 'wrong_size': m['files'][0]['bytes'] += 1
+    if case == 'wrong_hash': m['files'][0]['sha256'] = '0' * 64
+    mf.write_text(json.dumps(m))
+
+
+results = {}
+for case in CASES:
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='gns-integrity-') as temp:
+        root = Path(temp) / 'publication'
+        shutil.copytree(HERE, root)
+        mutate(root, case)
+        row = {}
+        for mode, flags in [('normal', []), ('optimized', ['-O'])]:
+            proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', *flags,
+                                   str(root / 'verify_publication.py'), '--integrity-only'],
+                                  cwd=temp, capture_output=True, check=False)
+            expected_accept = case == 'intact'
+            if (proc.returncode == 0) != expected_accept:
+                raise RuntimeError(case + ' ' + mode + ': unexpected acceptance/rejection')
+            row[mode] = 'ACCEPT' if proc.returncode == 0 else 'REJECT'
+        results[case] = row
+print(json.dumps({'result': 'PASS', 'negative_cases': len(CASES) - 1,
+                  'normal_and_optimized': True, 'controls': results}, sort_keys=True))

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Strict publication integrity and replay checks; Python standard library."""
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+MANIFEST = 'PUBLICATION_MANIFEST.json'
+EXPECTED = {
+    'CURRENT_SOURCE_AUDIT.md',
+    'PUBLICATION.json',
+    'PUBLICATION.md',
+    'README.md',
+    'audit/AUDIT.md',
+    'audit/AUDIT_RESULT.json',
+    'audit/AUDIT_SHA256SUMS.json',
+    'audit/AUDIT_SOURCE_METADATA.json',
+    'audit/CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_REPLAY.json',
+    'audit/CANDIDATE_REPLAY.json',
+    'audit/CORRECTIONS.md',
+    'audit/INDEPENDENT_RESULTS.json',
+    'audit/INPUT_BINDING.json',
+    'audit/verify_audit.py',
+    'audit/verify_independent.py',
+    'packet/CONTROL_RESULTS.json',
+    'packet/PROOF.md',
+    'packet/README.md',
+    'packet/REPOSITORY_GATE.json',
+    'packet/RESEARCH_LOG.md',
+    'packet/SHA256SUMS.json',
+    'packet/SOURCE_CHECK.json',
+    'packet/SOURCE_GATE.md',
+    'packet/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json',
+    'packet/STATUS.json',
+    'packet/turns.jsonl',
+    'packet/verify.py',
+    'packet/verify_manifest.py',
+    'publication.log',
+    'publication/gns_generation_counterexample.pdf',
+    'publication/gns_generation_counterexample.tex',
+    'publication/gns_verification.zip',
+    'publication/zenodo-deposit.json',
+    'test_integrity.py',
+    'verify_publication.py',
+}
+FROZEN_MANIFESTS = {
+    'packet/SHA256SUMS.json': 'a99e4e28c91d7f51ed116f868a698e2d718fec97a4ee82cf5b94aba409100f98',
+    'audit/AUDIT_SHA256SUMS.json': 'b0485e8e9a11aacfb567ad76bfb47614cebb06d4336b845939232c96427b69d3',
+}
+
+def require(condition, message):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def unique_pairs(pairs):
+    result = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        require(key not in result, 'duplicate JSON key: ' + key)
+        result[key] = value
+    return result
+
+
+def integrity():
+    paths = list(HERE.rglob('*'))
+    require(not any(p.is_symlink() for p in paths), 'symlink in publication')
+    actual = {p.relative_to(HERE).as_posix() for p in paths if p.is_file()}
+    require(actual == EXPECTED | {MANIFEST}, 'publication file set mismatch')
+    dirs = {p.relative_to(HERE).as_posix() for p in paths if p.is_dir()}
+    require(dirs == {'packet', 'audit', 'publication'}, 'publication directory set mismatch')
+    m = json.loads((HERE / MANIFEST).read_text(), object_pairs_hook=unique_pairs)
+    require(type(m) is dict and set(m) == {'schema', 'files'}, 'manifest schema')
+    require(m['schema'] == 'math-research-publication-v1', 'manifest version')
+    require(type(m['files']) is list and len(m['files']) == len(EXPECTED), 'manifest inventory count')
+    names = set()
+    for entry in m['files']:
+        require(type(entry) is dict and set(entry) == {'path', 'bytes', 'sha256'}, 'entry schema')
+        name = entry['path']
+        require(type(name) is str, 'path type')
+        pure = PurePosixPath(name)
+        require(not pure.is_absolute() and name == pure.as_posix() and '..' not in pure.parts
+                and '\\' not in name and name in EXPECTED, 'unsafe or unexpected path')
+        require(name not in names, 'duplicate manifest entry')
+        names.add(name)
+        require(type(entry['bytes']) is int and entry['bytes'] >= 0, 'invalid byte count')
+        require(type(entry['sha256']) is str and re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', entry['sha256']), 'invalid SHA-256')
+        data = (HERE / name).read_bytes()
+        require(len(data) == entry['bytes'], name + ': byte count mismatch')
+        require(hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() == entry['sha256'], name + ': SHA-256 mismatch')
+    require(names == EXPECTED, 'manifest names mismatch')
+    for name, expected in FROZEN_MANIFESTS.items():
+        require(hashlib.sha256((HERE / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == expected, 'frozen manifest changed: ' + name)
+    for manifest in FROZEN_MANIFESTS:
+        group = manifest.split('/')[0]
+        pinned = json.loads((HERE / manifest).read_text(), object_pairs_hook=unique_pairs)
+        require(type(pinned) is dict and len(pinned) == (12 if group == 'packet' else 10), 'frozen inventory count')
+        for leaf, entry in pinned.items():
+            require(type(leaf) is str and '/' not in leaf and '\\' not in leaf and leaf not in {'', '.', '..'}, 'frozen leaf')
+            require(type(entry) is dict and set(entry) == {'bytes', 'sha256'}, 'frozen entry schema')
+            data = (HERE / group / leaf).read_bytes()
+            require(len(data) == entry['bytes'] and hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() == entry['sha256'], 'frozen input changed: ' + group + '/' + leaf)
+    return {'integrity': 'PASS', 'manifested_files': len(EXPECTED), 'total_artifact_files': len(EXPECTED) + 1}
+
+
+def run(script, *args):
+    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', str(HERE / script), *args],
+                          cwd=HERE, capture_output=True, check=False)
+    require(proc.returncode == 0, script + ' failed: ' + proc.stderr.decode(errors='replace'))
+    return proc.stdout
+
+
+def main():
+    require(sys.argv[1:] in [[], ['--integrity-only']], 'usage: verify_publication.py [--integrity-only]')
+    result = integrity()
+    if not sys.argv[1:]:
+        author = run('packet/verify.py')
+        independent = run('audit/verify_independent.py')
+        require(author == (HERE / 'packet/CONTROL_RESULTS.json').read_bytes(), 'author replay output differs')
+        require(author == (HERE / 'audit/CANDIDATE_REPLAY.json').read_bytes(), 'audit author replay differs')
+        require(independent == (HERE / 'audit/INDEPENDENT_RESULTS.json').read_bytes(), 'independent replay output differs')
+        packet_integrity = json.loads(run('packet/verify_manifest.py'))
+        audit_integrity = json.loads(run('audit/verify_audit.py', str(HERE / 'packet')))
+        result.update(author_assertions=json.loads(author)['exact_assertions'],
+                      independent_assertions=json.loads(independent)['independent_assertions'],
+                      byte_identical_replays=True,
+                      packet_integrity=packet_integrity, audit_integrity=audit_integrity)
+    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()
